claim: For five voters with strict single-peaked rankings on the ordered alternatives \(0,1,\ldots,m-1\), each approving exactly their top \(k\) alternatives, a unique top-\(k\)-approval winner exists for some profile if and only if \(m\ge 2k-1\). Over all such profiles with a unique winner \(w\), the maximum distance from the median peak \(h\) is \[D_5(m,k)=\max |w-h|=\begin{cases}k-1,&2k-1\le m<5k-1,\m-3k,&m\ge5k-1.\end{cases}\]

limitations: Strict single-peaked rankings and exactly k top-ranked approvals.
Unique winner only; no tie-breaking extension.
title: A sharp five-voter displacement law for top-\(k\) approval under single-peaked preferences
